newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-BHP slips as analysts assess 1st half.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-BHP slips as analysts assess 1st half.

text.p: The shares of The Broken Hill Proprietary Co Ltd (BHP) reversed their early rise on Friday following the release of the company's results as some analysts assessed the result as disappointing.

At 12.05 p.m. (0105 GMT), BHP stock was 17 cents higher at A$17.22, from A$17.45 just before the result was announced at 0032 GMT. It reached a high of A$17.59 shortly after the company's shares resumed trading.
"It (the result) was obviously disappointing," said Eric Gale, director of institutions at Sydney broker, Ord Minnett.
Gale said most areas of the company's operations were lower in the second quarter, notably the petroleum division.
BHP reported a 9.8 percent fall in its first half earnings to A$790 million which included an abnormal gain of A$107 million.
Analysts estimates for BHP's first half net profit before abnormals had ranged from as low as A$600 million to as high as A$800 million.
BHP said pre-abnormal earnings for its petroleum divsion fell to A$146 million in the second quarter from A$189 million in the first quarter of 1996/97.
The company said the fall was primarily due to higher exploration expenses and the write-down of its Wyoming assets.
"The initial reaction (to the result) was positive but this has been followed by disappointment," said Phillip Toop, a dealer at Brisbane broker, Lance Jones.
Toop said because BHP was such a complex company it took time for the market to come to a consensus about the data.
"The day is still young. It could end at A$17.00 or A$17.50 depending on what the market thinks," he said.
